problem-game-story.alt: Problems Everywhere. AJ is moving through the day with Nia and Malik, and the first thing they notice is the same thing every sharp kid eventually notices: the world is full of problems waiting to be solved. AJ treats that like a map. Nia treats it like evidence. Malik treats it like a system. Some problems are small, some are huge.
problem-game-story.title: Problems Everywhere
problem-game-story.caption: AJ is moving through the day with Nia and Malik, and the first thing they notice is the same thing every sharp kid eventually notices: the world is full of problems waiting to be solved.

problem-game-story.alt: The Secret. Nia spots the pattern first: the people who make the most money, have the most impact, and live the most interesting lives are the ones who get really good at solving problems. Malik nods because the pattern shows up everywhere once you know how to look. That's the secret.
problem-game-story.title: The Secret
problem-game-story.caption: Nia spots the pattern first: the people who make the most money, have the most impact, and live the most interesting lives are the ones who get really good at solving problems.

problem-game-story.alt: Simple Problems. AJ sees the simple version first. Somebody's hungry? That's a problem. Make them food, problem solved. Small reward, but real value created. Nia calls it proof that useful work compounds.
problem-game-story.title: Simple Problems
problem-game-story.caption: AJ sees the simple version first.

problem-game-story.alt: Medium Problems. Malik points to the next level up: a business needs a website. That's a bigger problem. Build it, problem solved. Bigger reward, more value created. Now AJ, Nia, and Malik are moving up.
problem-game-story.title: Medium Problems
problem-game-story.caption: Malik points to the next level up: a business needs a website.

problem-game-story.alt: Hard Problems. By the time AJ, Nia, and Malik get to the hard problems, the stakes are clear. A community needs better education? That's a hard problem. Solve it and you get massive reward, massive impact. The harder the problem you can solve, the bigger the reward. Simple as that.
problem-game-story.title: Hard Problems
problem-game-story.caption: By the time AJ, Nia, and Malik get to the hard problems, the stakes are clear.

ai-revolution-story.alt: The Old Way. AJ, Nia, and Malik can feel the weight of the old system: solving hard problems used to require years of education, expensive degrees, and lucky opportunities. Nia sees the gatekeeping immediately. Malik sees the wasted potential. That was the old game, and the deck was stacked against most people.
ai-revolution-story.title: The Old Way
ai-revolution-story.caption: AJ, Nia, and Malik can feel the weight of the old system: solving hard problems used to require years of education, expensive degrees, and lucky opportunities.

ai-revolution-story.alt: Years of School. First you needed years of school. Then an expensive degree. Then you had to hope for a lucky opportunity. AJ sees why so many people got locked out before they ever got a chance to solve the problem.
ai-revolution-story.title: Years of School
ai-revolution-story.caption: First you needed years of school.

ai-revolution-story.alt: The New Way. Then AJ catches the shift. AI changes everything. Now the path is shorter. You see a problem, you ask questions, you use AI, you build a solution. Nia likes that it rewards thinking. Malik likes that it lowers the technical barrier.
ai-revolution-story.title: The New Way
ai-revolution-story.caption: Then AJ catches the shift.

ai-revolution-story.alt: The Real Skill. AJ knows the real move is not just having answers. AI is like having access to all the world's knowledge. But knowledge alone doesn't solve problems. The real skill is knowing what questions to ask. Nia hears the weak reasoning before it finishes. That's what separates problem solvers from everyone else.
ai-revolution-story.title: The Real Skill
ai-revolution-story.caption: AJ knows the real move is not just having answers.

ai-revolution-story.alt: Infinitely Patient Teacher. AJ, Nia, and Malik realize the wild part: AI never gets tired of your questions. It never gets irritated. Ask it a thousand questions in a row and it doesn't care. For the first time in history, you have access to an infinitely patient teacher.
ai-revolution-story.title: Infinitely Patient Teacher
ai-revolution-story.caption: AJ, Nia, and Malik realize the wild part: AI never gets tired of your questions.

ai-revolution-story.alt: Your New Superpower. This is revolutionary. AJ uses it to move faster, Nia uses it to sharpen judgment, and Malik uses it to test ideas and build. All you need is curiosity and the willingness to ask questions. That's your new superpower.
ai-revolution-story.title: Your New Superpower
ai-revolution-story.caption: This is revolutionary.

six-levels-story.alt: Most People Stop Here. AJ watches people stop after one or two questions and act like the answer is enough. Nia rolls her eyes because she can already hear the gaps. Malik stays quiet and watches the structure underneath. They're swimming at the surface while the real insights are deep below.
six-levels-story.title: Most People Stop Here
six-levels-story.caption: AJ watches people stop after one or two questions and act like the answer is enough.

six-levels-story.alt: Level 1: Why?. AJ starts the climb with a real example. A business is struggling. Level one: why is the business struggling? Answer: because they don't have enough customers. Nia says that's only the first door. Most people would stop here. Not AJ.
six-levels-story.title: Level 1: Why?
six-levels-story.caption: AJ starts the climb with a real example.

six-levels-story.alt: Level 2: Why?. AJ keeps going. Why don't they have enough customers? Answer: because people don't know about them. Malik sees the connection and keeps the graph moving. Keep asking.
six-levels-story.title: Level 2: Why?
six-levels-story.caption: AJ keeps going.

six-levels-story.alt: Level 3: Why?. Level three: why don't people know about them? Answer: because they have no online presence. Nia spots the real shape of the problem now. AJ and Malik can finally see it too.
six-levels-story.title: Level 3: Why?
six-levels-story.caption: Level three: why don't people know about them? Answer: because they have no online presence.

six-levels-story.alt: Levels 4 & 5: Going Deeper. Levels four and five hit the root. Why no online presence? Because they don't know how to build one. Why not? Because it seems too technical and expensive. Malik knows the hesitation is real, but the graph keeps pushing deeper.
six-levels-story.title: Levels 4 & 5: Going Deeper
six-levels-story.caption: Levels four and five hit the root.

six-levels-story.alt: Level 6: The Real Problem. Level six is the one that lands. Why does it seem too technical and expensive? Because they don't know about AI tools that make it easy and free. AJ sees the opening, Nia sees the logic, and Malik sees the toolchain. Now they have found a problem they can actually solve!
six-levels-story.title: Level 6: The Real Problem
six-levels-story.caption: Level six is the one that lands.

six-levels-story.alt: The Key Insight. AJ understands the takeaway now: if you can get just two or three levels deeper than most people, you're already ahead of ninety-nine percent of the world. Nia says that's where weak reasoning falls apart. Malik says that's where the real pattern shows up.
six-levels-story.title: The Key Insight
six-levels-story.caption: AJ understands the takeaway now: if you can get just two or three levels deeper than most people, you're already ahead of ninety-nine percent of the world.
